cards.explanation: The answer is Sihon king of Heshbon. The LORD tells Moses to cross the Arnon Valley and says, “See, I have delivered into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land.” Sihon is the first king Moses names in this retelling, friends. Og, king of Bashan, comes later in the passage.

The answer is False. The LORD tells Israel, “Begin to take possession of it and engage him in battle.” That's a very different instruction from the ones about Esau's descendants (Deuteronomy 2:4-5) and Moab (Deuteronomy 2:9), where Israel was told not to provoke them. Same road, different orders.

The answer is that they will tremble in anguish. The LORD says, “They will hear the reports of you and tremble in anguish because of you.” Hearing the reports is enough to shake them, friends. You know when a boss's reputation walks into the room before he does, and everybody is already sitting up straight? And notice the LORD says this very day He begins to put that dread and fear on them.

The answer is an offer of peace. Moses says, “So from the Wilderness of Kedemoth I sent messengers with an offer of peace to Sihon king of Heshbon…” The LORD had already told Israel to engage Sihon in battle (Deuteronomy 2:24), and still the messengers go out with an offer of peace. They show up with an open hand, friends.

The answer is to pay for it in silver. Moses says, “You can sell us food to eat and water to drink in exchange for silver.” They aren't asking for a handout, friends, they're asking to be customers. Everybody likes the customer who shows up with exact change.

The answer is True. Moses says Israel is asking to pass through “…just as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for us…” He's pointing to others who already said yes. It's like telling a shop owner, "Everybody else on this street already let me in."

The answer is that he won't let them pass through. Moses says, “But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through…” Pay in silver, stay on the road, and it was still a no. I once had somebody turn down a free cookie, friends, and even that doesn't compare.

The answer is stubborn. Moses says, “…the LORD your God had made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate, that He might deliver him into your hand…” So Moses gives that as the reason Sihon refused, friends. Take the words just as they stand.

The answer is True. Moses says, “And the LORD our God delivered him over to us, and we defeated him and his sons and his whole army.” Notice who he credits first, friends: the LORD our God delivered him. The whole army and his sons are included.

The answer is only the livestock and the plunder. Moses says, “We carried off for ourselves only the livestock and the plunder from the cities we captured.” The word "only" matters here. I think this is a heavy part of the story, friends, and Moses doesn't hurry past it.

The answer is walls. Moses says, “From Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, along with the city in the valley, even as far as Gilead, not one city had walls too high for us.” Then he adds, “The LORD our God gave us all of them.” High walls didn't stop what the LORD had given them, friends.

The answer is False. Moses says, “But you did not go near the land of the Ammonites, or the land along the banks of the Jabbok River…” These were places the LORD our God had forbidden. Israel took what it was given and left the rest alone, friends.

The answer is, "Do not fear him." The LORD says, “Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand…” Og, king of Bashan, is coming with his whole army, and the first thing the LORD speaks is "Do not fear…" That is a good first thing to hear, friends, even when the news is loud.

The answer is land. The LORD says, “…I have delivered him into your hand, along with all his people and his land.” The people and the land both come with the king, friends. It's the same word He used about Sihon earlier.

The answer is sixty. Moses says, “At that time we captured all sixty of his cities.” Sixty cities in the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan. That's a lot of doors, friends, and Moses counts every one.
The answer is False. Moses says, “There was not a single city we failed to take…” Walls, gates and bars didn't change that, friends. Not one was left out.

The answer is Mount Hermon. Moses says, “At that time we took from the two kings of the Amorites the land across the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley as far as Mount Hermon…” The two kings are Sihon and Og, friends. That's the whole stretch of land Moses is summing up.

The answer is iron. The text says, “His bed of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits wide, is still in Rabbah of the Ammonites.” It also says Og was the only one left of the remnant of the Rephaim. Nine cubits long and four wide, and made of iron. I slept on a pile of takeout menus in a junk drawer, friends, so that's a big step up from my bed.
